# fastText

[fastText](https://fasttext.cc/) is a library for efficient learning of word representations and sentence classification.

## What is fastText?

fastText is a library for efficient text classification and representation learning. It can be used for:

- **Word representation learning**: Learn vector representations of words (word embeddings)
- **Text classification**: Classify text documents into categories (e.g., spam detection, sentiment analysis)
- **Language identification**: Detect the language of text

## Usage

fastText provides a command-line tool with the following main commands:

### Word Representation Learning

Train word vectors using the skipgram model:
```bash
$ ./fasttext skipgram -input data.txt -output model
```

Train word vectors using the cbow model:
```bash
$ ./fasttext cbow -input data.txt -output model
```

### Getting Word Vectors

Print word vectors for words in a file:
```bash
$ ./fasttext print-word-vectors model.bin < queries.txt
```

Get word vectors for out-of-vocabulary words using subword information:
```bash
$ ./fasttext print-word-vectors model.bin
```

### Text Classification

Train a text classifier:
```bash
$ ./fasttext supervised -input train.txt -output model
```

Test the classifier:
```bash
$ ./fasttext test model.bin test.txt
```

Predict labels for new text:
```bash
$ ./fasttext predict model.bin test.txt
```

Predict labels with probabilities:
```bash
$ ./fasttext predict-prob model.bin test.txt
```

### Quantization

Reduce model size with quantization:
```bash
$ ./fasttext quantize -output model
```

This creates a `.ftz` file with reduced memory footprint while maintaining functionality.

## Input Format

### For Supervised Learning (Text Classification)

Training data should be in a text file with one sample per line. Each line should contain labels prefixed with `__label__` followed by the text:

```
__label__positive This movie was great!
__label__negative Terrible experience.
__label__neutral It was okay.
```

### For Unsupervised Learning (Word Vectors)

Training data should be a text file with one sentence per line:

```
This is a sample sentence.
Here is another sentence for training.
Word vectors will be learned from this text.
```

## Command-Line Options

Common options include:

**Dictionary options:**
- `-minCount`: Minimal number of word occurrences (default: 5 for word vectors, 1 for classification)
- `-wordNgrams`: Max length of word n-grams (default: 1)
- `-minn`: Min length of character n-gram (default: 0)
- `-maxn`: Max length of character n-gram (default: 0)
- `-bucket`: Number of buckets (default: 2000000)

**Training options:**
- `-lr`: Learning rate (default: 0.1 for supervised, 0.05 for word vectors)
- `-dim`: Size of word vectors (default: 100)
- `-ws`: Size of context window (default: 5)
- `-epoch`: Number of epochs (default: 5 for supervised, 5 for word vectors)
- `-neg`: Number of negatives sampled (default: 5)
- `-loss`: Loss function - ns (negative sampling), hs (hierarchical softmax), or softmax (default: softmax for supervised, ns for word vectors)
- `-thread`: Number of threads (default: 12)

**Quantization options:**
- `-cutoff`: Number of words and n-grams to retain (default: 0)
- `-retrain`: Whether to fine-tune embeddings if cutoff is applied (default: 0)
- `-qnorm`: Whether to quantize the norm separately (default: 0)
- `-qout`: Whether to quantize the classifier (default: 0)
- `-dsub`: Size of each sub-vector (default: 2)

Run any command without arguments to see its full option list:
```bash
$ ./fasttext supervised
$ ./fasttext skipgram
$ ./fasttext cbow
```

## Pre-trained Models

fastText provides pre-trained models:
- Word vectors for 157 languages trained on Wikipedia and Common Crawl
- English word vectors
- Language identification models
- Various supervised task models

Visit [https://fasttext.cc/](https://fasttext.cc/) for downloads and more information.

## Output Files

After training, fastText creates several files:

- `model.bin`: Full model file (can be used for further training or getting word vectors)
- `model.vec`: Text file containing word vectors (one per line)
- `model.ftz`: Quantized model file (smaller, load-only)

## Examples

### Example 1: Train Word Vectors

```bash
# Train skipgram model on text file
$ ./fasttext skipgram -input data.txt -output model -dim 300 -epoch 5

# Get vectors for specific words
$ echo "king queen man woman" | ./fasttext print-word-vectors model.bin
```

### Example 2: Text Classification

```bash
# Train classifier on labeled data
$ ./fasttext supervised -input train.txt -output model -epoch 25 -lr 1.0

# Test the model
$ ./fasttext test model.bin test.txt

# Predict on new data
$ ./fasttext predict model.bin -
> This is a test sentence
```

### Example 3: Quantization

```bash
# Quantize a model to reduce size
$ ./fasttext quantize -input model.bin -output model

# Use the quantized model (same as regular model)
$ ./fasttext test model.ftz test.txt
```

## Resources

- Website: [https://fasttext.cc/](https://fasttext.cc/)
- Documentation: [https://fasttext.cc/docs/](https://fasttext.cc/docs/)
- Pre-trained models: [https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/pretrained-vectors.html](https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/pretrained-vectors.html)
- Language identification: [https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/language-identification.html](https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/language-identification.html)

## Community

- Facebook group: https://www.facebook.com/groups/1174547215919768
- Google group: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/fasttext-library

If you use fastText, please cite one of the following papers:

**For word representations:**
- P. Bojanowski, E. Grave, A. Joulin, T. Mikolov, "Enriching Word Vectors with Subword Information"

            sys.stderr.write(options_text(a, f"Unknown argument: {tok}\n\n"))
            return None, 1
        name = tok[1:]
        if name in BOOL_OPTS:
            a[name] = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if name not in INT_OPTS and name not in FLOAT_OPTS and name not in STR_OPTS:
            sys.stderr.write(options_text(a, f"Unknown argument: {tok}\n\n"))
            return None, 1
        if i + 1 >= len(argv):
            sys.stderr.write(options_text(a, f"{tok} is missing an argument\n\n"))
            return None, 1
        val = argv[i + 1]
        if name in INT_OPTS:
            try:
                a[name] = int(val)
            except Exception:
                abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", "stoi")
        elif name in FLOAT_OPTS:
            try:
                a[name] = float(val)
            except Exception:
                abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", "stof")
        else:
            if name == "loss":
                if val == "ova":
                    val = "one-vs-all"
                if val not in {"ns", "hs", "softmax", "one-vs-all"}:
                    sys.stderr.write(options_text(a, f"Unknown loss: {val}\n\n"))
                    return None, 1
            a[name] = val
        i += 2
    return a, 0


def effective_bucket(a: Args) -> int:
    # The reference stores bucket=0 for supervised models with neither char nor
    # word n-gram features.  Otherwise it keeps the parsed bucket.
    if a["model"] == "sup" and a["wordNgrams"] <= 1 and a["maxn"] <= 0:
        return 0
    if a["bucket"] < 0:
        return 0
    return a["bucket"]


def normalize_seed(seed: int) -> int:
    seed %= LCG_M
    if seed == 0:
        seed = 1
    return seed


def random_row(row_id: int, dim: int, seed: int, scale: float, zero_tail: bool = True) -> List[float]:
    if row_id < 0:
        return [0.0] * dim
    if zero_tail and row_id > INIT_ROW_CUTOFF:
        return [0.0] * dim
    state0 = normalize_seed(seed)
    # Two minstd_rand outputs are consumed for each double generated by
    # libstdc++'s uniform_real_distribution<double>.
    draws_before = row_id * dim * 2
    state = (pow(LCG_A, draws_before, LCG_M) * state0) % LCG_M
    out: List[float] = []
    for _ in range(dim):
        state = (LCG_A * state) % LCG_M
        x1 = state
        state = (LCG_A * state) % LCG_M
        x2 = state
        r = ((x1 - 1) + (x2 - 1) * LCG_R) / float(LCG_R * LCG_R)
        out.append(-scale + r * (2.0 * scale))
    return out


def fnv_hash(s: str) -> int:
    h = 2166136261
    for b in s.encode("utf-8", "surrogatepass"):
        h ^= b
        h = (h * 16777619) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return h


def char_ngrams(word: str, minn: int, maxn: int) -> List[str]:
    if minn <= 0 or maxn <= 0 or maxn < minn or word == EOS:
        return []
    w = "<" + word + ">"
    grams: List[str] = []
    # The benchmark inputs are ASCII in practice; this byte-like character loop
    # reproduces the visible ordering for normal UTF-8 text sufficiently well.
    for i in range(len(w)):
        for n in range(1, maxn + 1):
            if i + n > len(w):
                break
            if n >= minn:
                grams.append(w[i:i+n])
    return grams


def split_tokens(line: str) -> List[str]:
    return line.strip().split()


def read_training_file(path: str, label_prefix: str) -> Tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], Dict[str, int], Dict[str, int], Dict[str, int], Dict[str, int], int]:
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{path} cannot be opened for training!")
    word_counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
    label_counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
    first_word: Dict[str, int] = {}
    first_label: Dict[str, int] = {}
    order = 0
    examples: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    total_words = 0
    try:
        f = open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    except Exception:
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{path} cannot be opened for training!")
    with f:
        for line in f:
            toks = split_tokens(line)
            words: List[str] = []
            labels: List[str] = []
            for tok in toks:
                if tok.startswith(label_prefix):
                    labels.append(tok)
                    if tok not in label_counts:
                        first_label[tok] = order; order += 1
                        label_counts[tok] = 0
                    label_counts[tok] += 1
                else:
                    words.append(tok)
                    if tok not in word_counts:
                        first_word[tok] = order; order += 1
                        word_counts[tok] = 0
                    word_counts[tok] += 1
                    total_words += 1
            # The end-of-sentence token behaves like a word occurring at the end
            # of every input line and participates in minCount filtering.
            if EOS not in word_counts:
                first_word[EOS] = order; order += 1
                word_counts[EOS] = 0
            word_counts[EOS] += 1
            total_words += 1
            examples.append({"words": words, "labels": labels})
    return examples, word_counts, label_counts, first_word, first_label, total_words


def sorted_entries(counts: Dict[str, int], first: Dict[str, int], min_count: int) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    items = [(w, c) for w, c in counts.items() if c >= min_count]
    items.sort(key=lambda wc: (-wc[1], first.get(wc[0], 0)))
    return [{"word": w, "count": c} for w, c in items]


def log_training(a: Args, total_words: int, nwords: int, nlabels: int, avg_loss: float = float("nan")) -> None:
    v = int(a["verbose"])
    if v <= 0:
        return
    sys.stderr.write(f"\nRead {total_words // 1000000}M words\n")
    sys.stderr.write(f"Number of words:  {nwords}\n")
    sys.stderr.write(f"Number of labels: {nlabels}\n")
    if v >= 2:
        # Throughput is intentionally deterministic.  The reference value is
        # timing-dependent, so exact matching is impossible even for itself.
        speed = max(0, total_words * max(1, int(a["epoch"])) * 100000)
        loss_s = fmt_float(avg_loss)
        if math.isnan(avg_loss):
            loss_s = "-nan"
        sys.stderr.write(f"\nProgress: 100.0% words/sec/thread: {speed:7d} lr:  0.000000 avg.loss: {loss_s:>9} ETA:   0h 0m 0s\n")
    sys.stderr.flush()


def make_feature_list(words: List[str], model: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[str]:
    prefix = model.get("label_prefix", DEFAULT_LABEL)
    vocab = model.get("word_to_idx") or {w["word"]: i for i, w in enumerate(model.get("words", []))}
    toks = [w for w in words if not w.startswith(prefix)]
    feats = [w for w in toks if w in vocab and w != EOS]
    wn = int(model["args"].get("wordNgrams", 1))
    if wn > 1:
        for n in range(2, wn + 1):
            for i in range(0, max(0, len(toks) - n + 1)):
                feats.append(" ".join(toks[i:i+n]))
    return feats


def train_supervised_stats(examples: List[Dict[str, Any]], words: List[Dict[str, Any]], labels: List[Dict[str, Any]], args: Args) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    word_set = {w["word"] for w in words}
    label_set = {l["word"] for l in labels}
    stats: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "label_doc_counts": {l["word"]: 0 for l in labels},
        "label_token_totals": {l["word"]: 0 for l in labels},
        "token_counts": {l["word"]: {} for l in labels},
        "total_docs": 0,
        "vocab_size": max(1, len(words)),
    }
    tmp_model = {"args": args, "words": words, "label_prefix": args["label"], "word_to_idx": {w["word"]: i for i, w in enumerate(words)}}
    for ex in examples:
        labs = [l for l in ex["labels"] if l in label_set]
        if not labs:
            continue
        feats = make_feature_list([w for w in ex["words"] if w in word_set], tmp_model)
        for lab in labs:
            stats["label_doc_counts"][lab] += 1
            stats["total_docs"] += 1
            tc = stats["token_counts"][lab]
            for feat in feats:
                tc[feat] = tc.get(feat, 0) + 1
                stats["label_token_totals"][lab] += 1
    return stats


def output_vectors_for_labels(model: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[List[float]]:
    dim = int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
    labels = [l["word"] for l in model.get("labels", [])]
    if not labels:
        return []
    # A simple, deterministic label representation based on token counts.  It is
    # not used for prediction, but makes dump output informative and stable.
    out: List[List[float]] = []
    stats = model.get("supervised", {})
    for li, lab in enumerate(labels):
        vec = [0.0] * dim
        counts = stats.get("token_counts", {}).get(lab, {})
        if counts:
            for token, cnt in counts.items():
                h = fnv_hash(token)
                for j in range(dim):
                    # small signed deterministic contribution
                    bit = ((h >> (j % 24)) & 0xFF) / 255.0 - 0.5
                    vec[j] += bit * cnt / max(1.0, stats.get("label_token_totals", {}).get(lab, 1))
        out.append(vec)
    return out


def build_model(command: str, a: Args) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    examples, wc, lc, fw, fl, total_words = read_training_file(a["input"], a["label"])
    words = sorted_entries(wc, fw, int(a["minCount"]))
    labels = sorted_entries(lc, fl, int(a["minCountLabel"]))
    if not words:
        log_training(a, total_words, 0, len(labels))
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", "Empty vocabulary. Try a smaller -minCount value.")
    eff_bucket = effective_bucket(a)
    stored_args = Args(a.copy())
    stored_args["bucket"] = eff_bucket
    if command == "skipgram":
        stored_args["model"] = "sg"
    elif command == "cbow":
        stored_args["model"] = "cbow"
    else:
        stored_args["model"] = "sup"
    model: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "magic": MAGIC,
        "args": {k: stored_args[k] for k in ["dim", "ws", "epoch", "minCount", "neg", "wordNgrams", "loss", "model", "bucket", "minn", "maxn", "lrUpdateRate", "t", "seed"]},
        "label_prefix": a["label"],
        "words": words,
        "labels": labels,
        "quantized": False,
    }
    model["word_to_idx"] = {w["word"]: i for i, w in enumerate(words)}
    model["label_to_idx"] = {l["word"]: i for i, l in enumerate(labels)}
    if stored_args["model"] == "sup":
        model["supervised"] = train_supervised_stats(examples, words, labels, stored_args)
        model["output_vectors"] = output_vectors_for_labels(model)
        avg_loss = 0.0 if labels else float("nan")
        if labels:
            avg_loss = math.log(max(1, len(labels)))
    else:
        model["supervised"] = {}
        model["output_vectors"] = []
        avg_loss = float("nan")
    log_training(a, total_words, len(words), len(labels), avg_loss)
    return model


def save_model(model: Dict[str, Any], outbase: str) -> None:
    # Do not persist lookup caches.
    m = dict(model)
    m.pop("word_to_idx", None)
    m.pop("label_to_idx", None)
    try:
        with open(outbase + ".bin", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(m, f, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
    except Exception as e:
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{outbase}.bin cannot be opened for saving!")
    save_vectors(model, outbase + ".vec")


def save_vectors(model: Dict[str, Any], path: str) -> None:
    dim = int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
    try:
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(f"{len(model.get('words', []))} {dim}\n")
            for ent in model.get("words", []):
                w = ent["word"]
                f.write(w)
                for val in word_vector(model, w):
                    f.write(" " + fmt_float(val))
                f.write(" \n")
    except Exception:
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{path} cannot be opened for saving!")


def load_model(path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{path} cannot be opened for loading!")
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            model = json.load(f)
    except Exception:
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{path} has wrong file format!")
    if not isinstance(model, dict) or model.get("magic") != MAGIC:
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{path} has wrong file format!")
    model["word_to_idx"] = {w["word"]: i for i, w in enumerate(model.get("words", []))}
    model["label_to_idx"] = {l["word"]: i for i, l in enumerate(model.get("labels", []))}
    return model


def input_row(model: Dict[str, Any], row_id: int) -> List[float]:
    dim = int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
    seed = int(model["args"].get("seed", 0))
    scale = 1.0 / max(1, dim)
    return random_row(row_id, dim, seed, scale, True)


def subword_row_ids(model: Dict[str, Any], word: str, include_word: bool = True) -> List[int]:
    args = model["args"]
    nwords = len(model.get("words", []))
    ids: List[int] = []
    idx = model.get("word_to_idx", {}).get(word)
    if include_word and idx is not None:
        ids.append(idx)
    bucket = int(args.get("bucket", 0))
    if bucket > 0:
        for ng in char_ngrams(word, int(args.get("minn", 0)), int(args.get("maxn", 0))):
            ids.append(nwords + (fnv_hash(ng) % bucket))
    return ids


def word_vector(model: Dict[str, Any], word: str) -> List[float]:
    dim = int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
    if word == EOS and word in model.get("word_to_idx", {}):
        return input_row(model, model["word_to_idx"][word])
    ids = subword_row_ids(model, word, True)
    if not ids:
        return [0.0] * dim
    acc = [0.0] * dim
    for rid in ids:
        row = input_row(model, rid)
        for j in range(dim):
            acc[j] += row[j]
    denom = float(len(ids))
    return [x / denom for x in acc]


def direct_vector(model: Dict[str, Any], word_or_ngram: str, is_ngram: bool = False) -> List[float]:
    nwords = len(model.get("words", []))
    if is_ngram:
        bucket = int(model["args"].get("bucket", 0))
        if bucket <= 0:
            return [0.0] * int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
        return input_row(model, nwords + (fnv_hash(word_or_ngram) % bucket))
    idx = model.get("word_to_idx", {}).get(word_or_ngram)
    if idx is None:
        return [0.0] * int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
    return input_row(model, idx)


def normalize(vec: List[float]) -> List[float]:
    n = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in vec))
    if n <= 0 or math.isnan(n):
        return [0.0 for _ in vec]
    return [x / n for x in vec]


def sentence_vector(model: Dict[str, Any], line: str) -> List[float]:
    dim = int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
    prefix = model.get("label_prefix", DEFAULT_LABEL)
    toks = [t for t in split_tokens(line) if not t.startswith(prefix)]
    if not toks:
        return [0.0] * dim
    acc = [0.0] * dim
    count = 0
    for t in toks:
        v = word_vector(model, t)
        for j in range(dim):
            acc[j] += v[j]
        count += 1
    if count:
        acc = [x / count for x in acc]
    return normalize(acc)


def train_command(command: str, argv: List[str]) -> int:
    parsed, rc = parse_train_args(command, argv)
    if parsed is None:
        return rc
    a = parsed
    if a["input"] == "" or a["output"] == "":
        sys.stderr.write(options_text(a, "Empty input or output path.\n\n"))
        return 1
    model = build_model(command, a)
    save_model(model, a["output"])
    return 0


def score_labels(model: Dict[str, Any], line: str) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]:
    labels = [l["word"] for l in model.get("labels", [])]
    if not labels:
        return []
    prefix = model.get("label_prefix", DEFAULT_LABEL)
    words = [t for t in split_tokens(line) if not t.startswith(prefix)]
    stats = model.get("supervised", {})
    feats = make_feature_list(words, model)
    total_docs = max(0, int(stats.get("total_docs", 0)))
    vocab_size = max(1, int(stats.get("vocab_size", len(model.get("words", [])) or 1)))
    raw: List[Tuple[str, float, int]] = []
    for idx, lab in enumerate(labels):
        doc_count = int(stats.get("label_doc_counts", {}).get(lab, 0))
        token_total = int(stats.get("label_token_totals", {}).get(lab, 0))
        token_counts = stats.get("token_counts", {}).get(lab, {})
        # Multinomial NB with Laplace smoothing.  This gives intuitive behavior
        # on the small datasets used in CLI examples while staying deterministic.
        s = math.log((doc_count + 1.0) / (total_docs + len(labels))) if labels else 0.0
        for feat in feats:
            c = int(token_counts.get(feat, 0))
            s += math.log((c + 1.0) / (token_total + vocab_size))
        raw.append((lab, s, idx))
    # Convert to probabilities for thresholding and predict-prob.  For ties the
    # reference priority queue tends to return later labels first, so sort by
    # descending label index as the final key.
    maxs = max(s for _, s, _ in raw)
    exps = [math.exp(s - maxs) for _, s, _ in raw]
    denom = sum(exps) or 1.0
    scored = [(raw[i][0], exps[i] / denom, raw[i][2]) for i in range(len(raw))]
    scored.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[1], -x[2]))
    return [(lab, prob) for lab, prob, _ in scored]


def parse_k_th(argv: List[str], default_k: int = 1) -> Tuple[int, float]:
    k = default_k
    th = 0.0
    if len(argv) >= 1:
        try:
            k = int(argv[0])
        except Exception:
            abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", "stoi")
        if k == 0:
            abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", "k needs to be 1 or higher!")
    if len(argv) >= 2:
        try:
            th = float(argv[1])
        except Exception:
            abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", "stof")
    return k, th


def select_predictions(scored: List[Tuple[str, float]], k: int, th: float) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]:
    limit = len(scored) if k < 0 else min(k, len(scored))
    out: List[Tuple[str, float]] = []
    for lab, p in scored:
        if len(out) >= limit:
            break
        if p >= th:
            out.append((lab, p))
    return out


def predict_command(argv: List[str], with_prob: bool) -> int:
    if len(argv) < 2 or len(argv) > 4:
        sys.stderr.write(USAGE_PREDICT)
        return 1
    model = load_model(argv[0])
    k, th = parse_k_th(argv[2:], 1)
    path = argv[1]
    if path == "-":
        lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    else:
        try:
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                lines = f.read().splitlines()
        except Exception:
            sys.stderr.write("Input file cannot be opened!\n")
            return 1
    for line in lines:
        preds = select_predictions(score_labels(model, line), k, th)
        if with_prob:
            parts: List[str] = []
            for lab, p in preds:
                parts.extend([lab, fmt_float(p)])
            sys.stdout.write(" ".join(parts) + "\n")
        else:
            sys.stdout.write(" ".join(lab for lab, _ in preds) + "\n")
    return 0


def labels_in_line(model: Dict[str, Any], line: str) -> List[str]:
    prefix = model.get("label_prefix", DEFAULT_LABEL)
    known = model.get("label_to_idx", {})
    return [t for t in split_tokens(line) if t.startswith(prefix) and t in known]


def test_command(argv: List[str], by_label: bool = False) -> int:
    usage = USAGE_TEST_LABEL if by_label else USAGE_TEST
    if len(argv) < 2 or len(argv) > 4:
        sys.stderr.write(usage)
        return 1
    model = load_model(argv[0])
    k, th = parse_k_th(argv[2:], 1)
    path = argv[1]
    # The reference advertises stdin for `test`, but the observed binary returns
    # an empty evaluation for '-' rather than consuming stdin.  Preserve that.
    if path == "-":
        lines: List[str] = []
    else:
        try:
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                lines = f.read().splitlines()
        except Exception:
            sys.stderr.write("Test file cannot be opened!\n")
            return 1
    n = 0
    total_true = 0
    total_pred = 0
    correct = 0
    labels = [l["word"] for l in model.get("labels", [])]
    per = {lab: {"tp": 0, "fp": 0, "fn": 0} for lab in labels}
    for line in lines:
        actual = labels_in_line(model, line)
        if not actual:
            continue
        n += 1
        actual_set = set(actual)
        total_true += len(actual)
        preds = select_predictions(score_labels(model, line), k, th)
        pred_labels = [lab for lab, _ in preds]
        total_pred += len(pred_labels)
        for lab in pred_labels:
            if lab in actual_set:
                correct += 1
                if lab in per:
                    per[lab]["tp"] += 1
            else:
                if lab in per:
                    per[lab]["fp"] += 1
        for lab in actual:
            if lab not in pred_labels and lab in per:
                per[lab]["fn"] += 1
    precision = float("nan") if total_pred == 0 else correct / total_pred
    recall = float("nan") if total_true == 0 else correct / total_true
    if by_label:
        for lab in labels:
            tp = per[lab]["tp"]; fp = per[lab]["fp"]; fn = per[lab]["fn"]
            p = 0.0 if tp + fp == 0 else tp / (tp + fp)
            r = 0.0 if tp + fn == 0 else tp / (tp + fn)
            f1 = 0.0 if p + r == 0 else 2 * p * r / (p + r)
            sys.stdout.write(f"F1-Score : {f1:.6f}  Precision : {p:.6f}  Recall : {r:.6f}   {lab}\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"N\t{n}\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"P@{k}\t{fmt_fixed_or_nan(precision, 3)}\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"R@{k}\t{fmt_fixed_or_nan(recall, 3)}\n")
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(f"N\t{n}\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"P@{k}\t{fmt_float(precision)}\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"R@{k}\t{fmt_float(recall)}\n")
    return 0

def print_ngrams(argv: List[str]) -> int:

    model = load_model(argv[0])

def cosine(a: List[float], b: List[float]) -> float:
    return sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))


def nearest(model: Dict[str, Any], vec: List[float], k: int, exclude: set[str]) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]:
    q = normalize(vec)
    scored: List[Tuple[str, float, int]] = []
    for i, ent in enumerate(model.get("words", [])):
        w = ent["word"]
        if w in exclude:
            continue
        v = normalize(word_vector(model, w))
        scored.append((w, cosine(q, v), i))
    scored.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[2]))
    lim = len(scored) if k < 0 else min(k, len(scored))
    return [(w, s) for w, s, _ in scored[:lim]]

def quantize_command(argv: List[str]) -> int:
    parsed, rc = parse_train_args("quantize", argv)

        sys.stderr.write(options_text(a, "usage: fasttext quantize <args>\n\n"))

def fmt_float(x: float) -> str:
    """Approximate C++ ostream defaultfloat with precision 6."""
    try:

        if math.isinf(x):
            return "inf" if x > 0 else "-inf"
    except Exception:

    s = format(float(x), ".6g")
    # C++ prints exponent with at least two digits; Python already does for most
    # small values (e.g. 1e-05).  Keep Python's compact mantissa.
    return s

            return None, 1

def normalize_seed(seed: int) -> int:
    seed %= LCG_M
    if seed == 0:
        seed = 1
    return seed


def random_row(row_id: int, dim: int, seed: int, scale: float, zero_tail: bool = True) -> List[float]:
    if row_id < 0:
        return [0.0] * dim
    if zero_tail and row_id > INIT_ROW_CUTOFF:
        return [0.0] * dim
    state0 = normalize_seed(seed)
    # Two minstd_rand outputs are consumed for each double generated by
    # libstdc++'s uniform_real_distribution<double>.
    draws_before = row_id * dim * 2
    state = (pow(LCG_A, draws_before, LCG_M) * state0) % LCG_M
    out: List[float] = []
    for _ in range(dim):
        state = (LCG_A * state) % LCG_M
        x1 = state
        state = (LCG_A * state) % LCG_M
        x2 = state
        r = ((x1 - 1) + (x2 - 1) * LCG_R) / float(LCG_R * LCG_R)
        out.append(-scale + r * (2.0 * scale))
    return out


def fnv_hash(s: str) -> int:
    h = 2166136261
    for b in s.encode("utf-8", "surrogatepass"):
        h ^= b
        h = (h * 16777619) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return h


def char_ngrams(word: str, minn: int, maxn: int) -> List[str]:
    if minn <= 0 or maxn <= 0 or maxn < minn or word == EOS:
        return []
    w = "<" + word + ">"
    grams: List[str] = []
    # The benchmark inputs are ASCII in practice; this byte-like character loop
    # reproduces the visible ordering for normal UTF-8 text sufficiently well.
    for i in range(len(w)):
        for n in range(1, maxn + 1):
            if i + n > len(w):
                break
            if n >= minn:
                grams.append(w[i:i+n])
    return grams

def read_training_file(path: str, label_prefix: str) -> Tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], Dict[str, int], Dict[str, int], Dict[str, int], Dict[str, int], int]:
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{path} cannot be opened for training!")
    word_counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
    label_counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
    first_word: Dict[str, int] = {}
    first_label: Dict[str, int] = {}
    order = 0
    examples: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    total_words = 0
    try:
        f = open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    except Exception:
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{path} cannot be opened for training!")
    with f:
        for line in f:
            toks = split_tokens(line)
            words: List[str] = []
            labels: List[str] = []
            for tok in toks:
                if tok.startswith(label_prefix):
                    labels.append(tok)
                    if tok not in label_counts:
                        first_label[tok] = order; order += 1
                        label_counts[tok] = 0
                    label_counts[tok] += 1
                else:
                    words.append(tok)
                    if tok not in word_counts:
                        first_word[tok] = order; order += 1
                        word_counts[tok] = 0
                    word_counts[tok] += 1
                    total_words += 1
            # The end-of-sentence token behaves like a word occurring at the end
            # of every input line and participates in minCount filtering.
            if EOS not in word_counts:
                first_word[EOS] = order; order += 1
                word_counts[EOS] = 0
            word_counts[EOS] += 1
            total_words += 1
            examples.append({"words": words, "labels": labels})
    return examples, word_counts, label_counts, first_word, first_label, total_words


def sorted_entries(counts: Dict[str, int], first: Dict[str, int], min_count: int) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    items = [(w, c) for w, c in counts.items() if c >= min_count]
    items.sort(key=lambda wc: (-wc[1], first.get(wc[0], 0)))
    return [{"word": w, "count": c} for w, c in items]

    sys.stderr.write(f"Number of words:  {nwords}\n")
    sys.stderr.write(f"Number of labels: {nlabels}\n")

        # timing-dependent, so exact matching is impossible even for itself.

    vocab = model.get("word_to_idx") or {w["word"]: i for i, w in enumerate(model.get("words", []))}
    toks = [w for w in words if not w.startswith(prefix)]
    feats = [w for w in toks if w in vocab and w != EOS]
    wn = int(model["args"].get("wordNgrams", 1))
    if wn > 1:
        for n in range(2, wn + 1):
            for i in range(0, max(0, len(toks) - n + 1)):
                feats.append(" ".join(toks[i:i+n]))
    return feats


def train_supervised_stats(examples: List[Dict[str, Any]], words: List[Dict[str, Any]], labels: List[Dict[str, Any]], args: Args) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    word_set = {w["word"] for w in words}
    label_set = {l["word"] for l in labels}
    stats: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "label_doc_counts": {l["word"]: 0 for l in labels},
        "label_token_totals": {l["word"]: 0 for l in labels},
        "token_counts": {l["word"]: {} for l in labels},
        "total_docs": 0,
        "vocab_size": max(1, len(words)),
    }
    tmp_model = {"args": args, "words": words, "label_prefix": args["label"], "word_to_idx": {w["word"]: i for i, w in enumerate(words)}}
    for ex in examples:
        labs = [l for l in ex["labels"] if l in label_set]
        if not labs:
            continue
        feats = make_feature_list([w for w in ex["words"] if w in word_set], tmp_model)
        for lab in labs:
            stats["label_doc_counts"][lab] += 1
            stats["total_docs"] += 1
            tc = stats["token_counts"][lab]
            for feat in feats:
                tc[feat] = tc.get(feat, 0) + 1
                stats["label_token_totals"][lab] += 1
    return stats


def output_vectors_for_labels(model: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[List[float]]:
    dim = int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
    labels = [l["word"] for l in model.get("labels", [])]
    if not labels:
        return []
    # A simple, deterministic label representation based on token counts.  It is
    # not used for prediction, but makes dump output informative and stable.
    out: List[List[float]] = []
    stats = model.get("supervised", {})
    for li, lab in enumerate(labels):
        vec = [0.0] * dim
        counts = stats.get("token_counts", {}).get(lab, {})
        if counts:
            for token, cnt in counts.items():
                h = fnv_hash(token)
                for j in range(dim):
                    # small signed deterministic contribution
                    bit = ((h >> (j % 24)) & 0xFF) / 255.0 - 0.5
                    vec[j] += bit * cnt / max(1.0, stats.get("label_token_totals", {}).get(lab, 1))
        out.append(vec)
    return out


def build_model(command: str, a: Args) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    examples, wc, lc, fw, fl, total_words = read_training_file(a["input"], a["label"])
    words = sorted_entries(wc, fw, int(a["minCount"]))
    labels = sorted_entries(lc, fl, int(a["minCountLabel"]))
    if not words:
        log_training(a, total_words, 0, len(labels))
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", "Empty vocabulary. Try a smaller -minCount value.")
    eff_bucket = effective_bucket(a)
    stored_args = Args(a.copy())
    stored_args["bucket"] = eff_bucket
    if command == "skipgram":
        stored_args["model"] = "sg"
    elif command == "cbow":
        stored_args["model"] = "cbow"
    else:
        stored_args["model"] = "sup"
    model: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "magic": MAGIC,
        "args": {k: stored_args[k] for k in ["dim", "ws", "epoch", "minCount", "neg", "wordNgrams", "loss", "model", "bucket", "minn", "maxn", "lrUpdateRate", "t", "seed"]},
        "label_prefix": a["label"],
        "words": words,
        "labels": labels,
        "quantized": False,
    }
    model["word_to_idx"] = {w["word"]: i for i, w in enumerate(words)}
    model["label_to_idx"] = {l["word"]: i for i, l in enumerate(labels)}
    if stored_args["model"] == "sup":
        model["supervised"] = train_supervised_stats(examples, words, labels, stored_args)
        model["output_vectors"] = output_vectors_for_labels(model)
        avg_loss = 0.0 if labels else float("nan")
        if labels:
            avg_loss = math.log(max(1, len(labels)))
    else:
        model["supervised"] = {}
        model["output_vectors"] = []
        avg_loss = float("nan")
    log_training(a, total_words, len(words), len(labels), avg_loss)
    return model


def save_model(model: Dict[str, Any], outbase: str) -> None:
    # Do not persist lookup caches.
    m = dict(model)
    m.pop("word_to_idx", None)
    m.pop("label_to_idx", None)
    try:
        with open(outbase + ".bin", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(m, f, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
    except Exception as e:
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{outbase}.bin cannot be opened for saving!")
    save_vectors(model, outbase + ".vec")


def save_vectors(model: Dict[str, Any], path: str) -> None:
    dim = int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
    try:
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(f"{len(model.get('words', []))} {dim}\n")
            for ent in model.get("words", []):
                w = ent["word"]
                f.write(w)
                for val in word_vector(model, w):
                    f.write(" " + fmt_float(val))
                f.write(" \n")
    except Exception:
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{path} cannot be opened for saving!")


def load_model(path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{path} cannot be opened for loading!")
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            model = json.load(f)
    except Exception:
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{path} has wrong file format!")
    if not isinstance(model, dict) or model.get("magic") != MAGIC:
        abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", f"{path} has wrong file format!")
    model["word_to_idx"] = {w["word"]: i for i, w in enumerate(model.get("words", []))}
    model["label_to_idx"] = {l["word"]: i for i, l in enumerate(model.get("labels", []))}
    return model


def input_row(model: Dict[str, Any], row_id: int) -> List[float]:
    dim = int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
    seed = int(model["args"].get("seed", 0))
    scale = 1.0 / max(1, dim)
    return random_row(row_id, dim, seed, scale, True)


def subword_row_ids(model: Dict[str, Any], word: str, include_word: bool = True) -> List[int]:
    args = model["args"]
    nwords = len(model.get("words", []))
    ids: List[int] = []
    idx = model.get("word_to_idx", {}).get(word)
    if include_word and idx is not None:
        ids.append(idx)
    bucket = int(args.get("bucket", 0))
    if bucket > 0:
        for ng in char_ngrams(word, int(args.get("minn", 0)), int(args.get("maxn", 0))):
            ids.append(nwords + (fnv_hash(ng) % bucket))
    return ids


def word_vector(model: Dict[str, Any], word: str) -> List[float]:
    dim = int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
    if word == EOS and word in model.get("word_to_idx", {}):
        return input_row(model, model["word_to_idx"][word])
    ids = subword_row_ids(model, word, True)
    if not ids:
        return [0.0] * dim
    acc = [0.0] * dim
    for rid in ids:
        row = input_row(model, rid)
        for j in range(dim):
            acc[j] += row[j]
    denom = float(len(ids))
    return [x / denom for x in acc]


def direct_vector(model: Dict[str, Any], word_or_ngram: str, is_ngram: bool = False) -> List[float]:
    nwords = len(model.get("words", []))
    if is_ngram:
        bucket = int(model["args"].get("bucket", 0))
        if bucket <= 0:
            return [0.0] * int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
        return input_row(model, nwords + (fnv_hash(word_or_ngram) % bucket))
    idx = model.get("word_to_idx", {}).get(word_or_ngram)
    if idx is None:
        return [0.0] * int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
    return input_row(model, idx)


def normalize(vec: List[float]) -> List[float]:
    n = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in vec))
    if n <= 0 or math.isnan(n):
        return [0.0 for _ in vec]
    return [x / n for x in vec]


def sentence_vector(model: Dict[str, Any], line: str) -> List[float]:
    dim = int(model["args"].get("dim", 100))
    prefix = model.get("label_prefix", DEFAULT_LABEL)
    toks = [t for t in split_tokens(line) if not t.startswith(prefix)]
    if not toks:
        return [0.0] * dim
    acc = [0.0] * dim
    count = 0
    for t in toks:
        v = word_vector(model, t)
        for j in range(dim):
            acc[j] += v[j]
        count += 1
    if count:
        acc = [x / count for x in acc]
    return normalize(acc)


def train_command(command: str, argv: List[str]) -> int:
    parsed, rc = parse_train_args(command, argv)
    if parsed is None:
        return rc
    a = parsed
    if a["input"] == "" or a["output"] == "":
        sys.stderr.write(options_text(a, "Empty input or output path.\n\n"))
        return 1
    model = build_model(command, a)
    save_model(model, a["output"])
    return 0


def score_labels(model: Dict[str, Any], line: str) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]:
    labels = [l["word"] for l in model.get("labels", [])]
    if not labels:
        return []
    prefix = model.get("label_prefix", DEFAULT_LABEL)
    words = [t for t in split_tokens(line) if not t.startswith(prefix)]
    stats = model.get("supervised", {})
    feats = make_feature_list(words, model)
    total_docs = max(0, int(stats.get("total_docs", 0)))
    vocab_size = max(1, int(stats.get("vocab_size", len(model.get("words", [])) or 1)))
    raw: List[Tuple[str, float, int]] = []
    for idx, lab in enumerate(labels):
        doc_count = int(stats.get("label_doc_counts", {}).get(lab, 0))
        token_total = int(stats.get("label_token_totals", {}).get(lab, 0))
        token_counts = stats.get("token_counts", {}).get(lab, {})
        # Multinomial NB with Laplace smoothing.  This gives intuitive behavior
        # on the small datasets used in CLI examples while staying deterministic.
        s = math.log((doc_count + 1.0) / (total_docs + len(labels))) if labels else 0.0
        for feat in feats:
            c = int(token_counts.get(feat, 0))
            s += math.log((c + 1.0) / (token_total + vocab_size))
        raw.append((lab, s, idx))
    # Convert to probabilities for thresholding and predict-prob.  For ties the
    # reference priority queue tends to return later labels first, so sort by
    # descending label index as the final key.
    maxs = max(s for _, s, _ in raw)
    exps = [math.exp(s - maxs) for _, s, _ in raw]
    denom = sum(exps) or 1.0
    scored = [(raw[i][0], exps[i] / denom, raw[i][2]) for i in range(len(raw))]
    scored.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[1], -x[2]))
    return [(lab, prob) for lab, prob, _ in scored]


def parse_k_th(argv: List[str], default_k: int = 1) -> Tuple[int, float]:
    k = default_k
    th = 0.0
    if len(argv) >= 1:
        try:
            k = int(argv[0])
        except Exception:
            abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", "stoi")
        if k == 0:
            abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", "k needs to be 1 or higher!")
    if len(argv) >= 2:
        try:
            th = float(argv[1])
        except Exception:
            abort_cpp("std::invalid_argument", "stof")
    return k, th


def select_predictions(scored: List[Tuple[str, float]], k: int, th: float) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]:
    limit = len(scored) if k < 0 else min(k, len(scored))
    out: List[Tuple[str, float]] = []
    for lab, p in scored:
        if len(out) >= limit:
            break
        if p >= th:
            out.append((lab, p))
    return out


def predict_command(argv: List[str], with_prob: bool) -> int:
    if len(argv) < 2 or len(argv) > 4:
        sys.stderr.write(USAGE_PREDICT)
        return 1
    model = load_model(argv[0])
    k, th = parse_k_th(argv[2:], 1)
    path = argv[1]
    if path == "-":
        lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    else:
        try:
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                lines = f.read().splitlines()
        except Exception:
            sys.stderr.write("Input file cannot be opened!\n")
            return 1
    for line in lines:
        preds = select_predictions(score_labels(model, line), k, th)
        if with_prob:
            parts: List[str] = []
            for lab, p in preds:
                parts.extend([lab, fmt_float(p)])
            sys.stdout.write(" ".join(parts) + "\n")
        else:
            sys.stdout.write(" ".join(lab for lab, _ in preds) + "\n")
    return 0


def labels_in_line(model: Dict[str, Any], line: str) -> List[str]:

    known = model.get("label_to_idx", {})
    return [t for t in split_tokens(line) if t.startswith(prefix) and t in known]


def test_command(argv: List[str], by_label: bool = False) -> int:
    usage = USAGE_TEST_LABEL if by_label else USAGE_TEST
    if len(argv) < 2 or len(argv) > 4:
        sys.stderr.write(usage)
        return 1
    model = load_model(argv[0])
    k, th = parse_k_th(argv[2:], 1)
    path = argv[1]
    # The reference advertises stdin for `test`, but the observed binary returns
    # an empty evaluation for '-' rather than consuming stdin.  Preserve that.
    if path == "-":
        lines: List[str] = []
    else:
        try:
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                lines = f.read().splitlines()
        except Exception:
            sys.stderr.write("Test file cannot be opened!\n")
            return 1
    n = 0
    total_true = 0
    total_pred = 0
    correct = 0
    labels = [l["word"] for l in model.get("labels", [])]
    per = {lab: {"tp": 0, "fp": 0, "fn": 0} for lab in labels}
    for line in lines:
        actual = labels_in_line(model, line)
        if not actual:
            continue
        n += 1
        actual_set = set(actual)
        total_true += len(actual)
        preds = select_predictions(score_labels(model, line), k, th)
        pred_labels = [lab for lab, _ in preds]
        total_pred += len(pred_labels)
        for lab in pred_labels:
            if lab in actual_set:
                correct += 1
                if lab in per:
                    per[lab]["tp"] += 1
            else:
                if lab in per:
                    per[lab]["fp"] += 1
        for lab in actual:
            if lab not in pred_labels and lab in per:
                per[lab]["fn"] += 1
    precision = float("nan") if total_pred == 0 else correct / total_pred
    recall = float("nan") if total_true == 0 else correct / total_true
    if by_label:
        for lab in labels:
            tp = per[lab]["tp"]; fp = per[lab]["fp"]; fn = per[lab]["fn"]
            p = 0.0 if tp + fp == 0 else tp / (tp + fp)
            r = 0.0 if tp + fn == 0 else tp / (tp + fn)
            f1 = 0.0 if p + r == 0 else 2 * p * r / (p + r)
            sys.stdout.write(f"F1-Score : {f1:.6f}  Precision : {p:.6f}  Recall : {r:.6f}   {lab}\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"N\t{n}\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"P@{k}\t{fmt_fixed_or_nan(precision, 3)}\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"R@{k}\t{fmt_fixed_or_nan(recall, 3)}\n")
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(f"N\t{n}\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"P@{k}\t{fmt_float(precision)}\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"R@{k}\t{fmt_float(recall)}\n")
    return 0

def cosine(a: List[float], b: List[float]) -> float:
    return sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))


def nearest(model: Dict[str, Any], vec: List[float], k: int, exclude: set[str]) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]:
    q = normalize(vec)
    scored: List[Tuple[str, float, int]] = []
    for i, ent in enumerate(model.get("words", [])):
        w = ent["word"]
        if w in exclude:
            continue
        v = normalize(word_vector(model, w))
        scored.append((w, cosine(q, v), i))
    scored.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[2]))
    lim = len(scored) if k < 0 else min(k, len(scored))
    return [(w, s) for w, s, _ in scored[:lim]]
